Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity throughput assessment

Hi Neha,

We spun up a self-serve project on Redwood and the metrics look promising — we'd like to move to a Dedicated footprint to meet predictable latency for production. Quick context: Helix Analytics processes high-frequency conversational queries for financial feeds. Typical prompt size is 400-800 tokens, but we do also have bursts with longer contexts up to ~2k tokens.

Can we schedule a technical-capacity demo to understand how Redwood Dedicated would support sustained throughput? Ballpark targets: steady-state ~2,000 tokens/sec sustained across 8 concurrent streams, p50 latency goal <120ms, p95 <300ms. We also need guidance on autoscale/burst behavior and quantization trade-offs.

Timezone: PST (Los Angeles). Prefer afternoons this week.

Thanks — happy to share an internal architecture note and some sample logs if helpful.

Anna Li
Senior Platform Engineer
Helix Analytics

- Expected concurrent sessions vs concurrent streams (you said 8 concurrent streams — is that 8 steady sessions or 8 parallel callers per shard?)
- Any throughput shape (steady vs spiky bursts; if spiky, typical duration)

Hi Neha — thanks for the quick reply.

Answers inline:
- Avg tokens: 450–700. Peaks: ~18% of requests run >1,500 tokens and ~3% hit ~2,000 tokens.
- Concurrent sessions: we expect ~200 user sessions generating ~8 steady parallel inference streams during peak; the product team expects to scale sessions to 1k over Q3. The 8 streams figure is per-region parallelism for our aggregators.
- Shape: Mostly steady during market hours with predictable 15–30 minute spikes at data release times. Bursts rarely exceed 6 minutes.

We prefer Wed 6/28 2:00–2:45pm PT if that slot is available — would like to invite our CTO, Tom Reynolds, to that meeting. Can you include an agenda and the worksheet you mentioned? Also please include the expected attendee list (runtime/solutions engineer recommended).

We generally want the session indexed to our needs: 1) sizing for current steady load + short bursts, 2) latency/99 tail behavior under burst, 3) failover strategy and routing during capacity constraints.

Thanks,
Anna
